correctness.rationale: The budget simplex is compact and a positive surviving tree count is feasible for m≥2, so allocations with any singular outage cofactor cannot maximize the objective. On the positive domain log of the worst tree count is the minimum of concave log determinants of affine reduced Laplacians and is therefore concave. Averaging over page permutations and hub interchange preserves budget and does not decrease it. For symmetric weights, direct tree counting gives the intact count 2^(m−1)a^m(ma+2b): a tree uses the hub edge and one spoke per page, or omits the hub edge and uses exactly one double-spoke connector page. Removing the hub sets b=0; removing one spoke instead forces its page to use the other spoke, giving 2^(m−2)a^m((m−1)a+2b). These outage counts tie at r=(m+1)/2. The budget substitutes a=B/(2m+tr). To the right of the tie the objective strictly decreases; on its left the derivative sign is that of 4m−(m²−1)t−2mtr. Its zero reaches the tie and zero precisely at the stated t1 and t2. This verifies the optimizer, optimum, active failures and both equality cases. For unrestricted uniqueness, the average of the spoke-outage log determinants is strictly concave on its positive domain: a zero log-det curvature direction would vanish on every undeleted-edge dyad sum; in a simple graph those dyads are independent by inspecting off-diagonals and then diagonals, so the different deletions admit no common nonzero null direction. If an optimal allocation were nonsymmetric, group averaging would strictly increase this spoke average. But the average is at least the worst-outage log determinant at the original allocation and equals it at the symmetric optimum, since spoke outage is active there in every regime. That is a contradiction, including at b=0 or either threshold. The intact scalar derivative has sign 4m−m(m+1)t−2mtr, giving the nominal threshold 4/(m+1) by the same concavity and symmetry reasoning. It is strictly below t2; the displayed limits follow directly.
residual_risks: Continuous nonnegative weights, t,B>0, m≥2 and exactly one adversarial designated edge deletion without reallocation. This is not random survival probability or a theorem about other graphs or multiple outages.

value.rationale: Worst single-outage tree connectivity is a natural robust analogue of an established continuous network-design measure. On an infinite graph family the theorem distinguishes equalized failure scenarios, an interior spoke-limited design and complete abandonment of the hub edge. Its exact price comparison isolates when backup remains worthwhile under the robust criterion but not without outages; proof of unrestricted uniqueness makes that interpretation independent of any symmetric-design restriction.
residual_risks: Relevance is to the specified determinant measure; no empirical reliability, general network topology or multiple-failure performance is proved.
